notes:
Access: potterybarn.com's /shop/* paths return Akamai 403 'Restricted Access' to plain HTTP (curl_cffi with chrome120 TLS impersonation reached only the homepage/robots.txt at tier 1) and to headless Playwright/Chromium (tier 2, blocked even on homepage). robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow. Reached all product-listing pages via Claude-in-Chrome (tier 3) with a real (non-headless) Chrome session. Note: this Chrome session is shared/contended across 10 concurrent workers this run, causing frequent tab-group resets; some sub-pages could not be re-verified before the shared session moved on (see flagged rows below).

Navigation discovery: main nav 'New' tab links to /shop/new/, whose SEO/OG url canonicalizes to /shop/new/bestsellers-all/ for a distinct 'Bestsellers' hub (breadcrumb 'New > Bestsellers', title 'Bestsellers | Pottery Barn') separate from /shop/new/all-new/ ('All New Arrivals'). The Bestsellers hub itself exposes 10 genuine site-defined children (department tiles + nav links, each its own dedicated PLP with its own breadcrumb/title, not just a filter): Furniture, Outdoor & Garden, Pillows & Decor, Bedding, Tabletop & Bar, Rug, Lighting, Bath, Art & Mirrors, Windows Bestsellers. Also checked footer, PDP 'Bestseller' badges (correctly excluded per brief - badge on a PDP is not a PLP), and site search (not needed, real nav already surfaced everything).

All rows below were opened and confirmed as real product-listing pages (browsable grid, filter/sort controls, 'Bestseller' badges on the listed products) - not editorial/marketing pages. qty for the aggregate + 5 department pages came from each page's own rendered '<Category> — N Items' header (screenshot/text-extracted directly, not a filter facet). The remaining 5 department pages (Rug, Lighting, Bath, Art & Mirrors, Windows Bestsellers) have confirmed genuine URLs (extracted live from the Bestsellers hub's own DOM links) but their exact rendered counts could not be captured before the shared Claude-in-Chrome session was reclaimed by other concurrent workers (tab-group repeatedly invalidated mid-sequence) - qty left null with a MANUAL REVIEW flag per the no-fabrication rule rather than guessed or copied from an unverified filter-facet number. One data point worth recording: a department filter-facet on the hub page showed 'Bath (109)' and 'Furniture (488)' - the Furniture facet figure (488) is measurably higher than that page's own confirmed rendered header (470), proving facet counts on this site can be inflated vs the true PLP header, so the Bath facet figure (109) was deliberately NOT used as qty.
